title: Erskine Hawkins, Dud Bascomb and who gets promoted
summary: Edison says Hawkins led on his chops and promotion, not talent, and complains talent matters little in today's industry.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Yes, he is. So I think after he heard what -- well, after I went to New York, I became so engrossed in listening to the solos, going from place to place. I used to go listen to Erskine Hawkins, go listen to Charlie Shavers, go listen to Roy Eldridge.
What did you think of Erskine Hawkins?

Well, he had a style. But the one I really liked in his band was Dud, Dud Bascomb. Now, he was fantastic. Well, it goes back to what you were asking me a while ago about Basie, how did Basie get the band? I wondered how Erskine Hawkins got the band.
Yes, that was just a matter of --
Yeah, see, that was a school band when it started, you know.
Yeah, but, you know, Erskine didn't
get -- sort of his trumpet playing precisely but he's a fine Nice man.

But if talent prevailed, he wouldn't be the band leader. If talent had prevailed, he wouldn't have been the band leader. Because he didn't have the talent to be a band leader -- he had the chops. He had fantastic chops. And that enabled him to be the band leader, too, because in those days playing high was -- reaching the stratosphere on your horn.
He played high but it wasn't very -- never very tasteful, was it.

No. And he was promoted, to, through the Gale Agency like the 20th century Gabriel, you know. He was promoted. In those days -- if they promoted jazz now like they did in those days, there wouldn't be no rock and roll. It would be strictly good music, you know. But I don't know -- I can't describe what's happening today with the industry. It's not what you can do, it's who you know. It's not how much you can do or how much talent you have, it's how little talent you have.
Yeah, how little talent you have. You don't have to be good now to make money. All you have to do is get somebody to say, 'I'm going to make a star out of you.' And
That's right. But why it always seems to have to be some nitwit --
Yeah. Well, I wanted to say that but I'm very glad you said it.
